meta.parties: John Singho v. Pedris Hamy Et Al

rules.statement: A Judge should not consider, without giving due notice to the parties, any matters in dispute that may appear to him to arise between them in the course of the proceedings when all parties agree on the points in dispute and state them to the Court.
rules.supporting_quote: "The positive will however be different when the points in dispute are not set down in the form of issues. A Judge may find it frequently very convenient to state, in the form of issues, the matters in dispute between the parties in a partition action. After satisfying himself that no person other than the parties to the action has interests in the property, he will in such a case decide the issues framed by him and enter a decree for partition or sale according to his finding on those issues. He should not in such circumstances consider, without giving due notice to the parties, any matters in dispute that may appear to him to arise between them in the course of the proceedings."
